title: Color correction and debanding function incorrectly when HDR 2D is enabled
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.2.stable.official [46dc27791], v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6], and current `master`

### System information

Godot v4.2.stable - Windows 10.0.26100 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6109) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 Threads)

### Issue description

It seems that the HDR 2D project setting causes nonlinear sRGB encoding to not be applied before the `Environment` color correction effect and the Debanding project setting (`rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_debanding`) are applied. This appears to cause some issues:

## Color Correction

If I apply the template 1D gradient and 3D LUT textures to a scene, I get a small change in original scene colour, but when HDR 2D is enabled I get much more significant and unexpected change in scene colour.

| LUT Applied | HDR 2D Disabled | HDR 2D Enabled
| --- | --- | ---
| None (Original Scene) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6504972-042f-44f0-8ceb-b08d85c166e3) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6504972-042f-44f0-8ceb-b08d85c166e3)
| [1D gradient template](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/_images/environment_adjustments_default_gradient.webp) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01409319-388a-4e56-b00a-ed9e3a53d5d7) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/057cb160-6f06-4f23-a79f-5026fbe263f1)
| [3D LUT template](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/_images/environment_adjustments_3d_lut_template.webp) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97f191d7-14f9-4518-b15d-a61422267090) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0fedb55-a5db-401f-8a37-dc84667ce320)

So let's say I use the color correction to adjust my scene by loading a screenshot of my game into an image editor and perform a colour replacement on the blue sky to make all blue colours yellowish orange:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70f91292-d150-45bc-8888-4203a94b84d9)
HDR 2D Disabled | HDR 2D Enabled
|--- | ---
| ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23de25b1-a589-4a62-ae9a-c4f3422c392a) | ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d2a5f5b-c1b8-4ca1-8b5f-1ae2ec3bf3ae)

As seen in the above screenshots, the HDR 2D project setting prevents my color correction adjustment from being applied correctly.

(Originally, I reported this in #107682, but it appears better to separate these into two separate issues.)

## Debanding

Another issue with the same root cause can be seen in the Debanding project setting (`rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_debanding`):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/051260a9-5c37-44a7-b34b-3abf71294748)

Zoomed in portion of above screenshot:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb012fed-8ecd-4c83-ad18-565f57241c03)

This issue is best seen with the lights turned out: extra noise that does not help with debanding is added to the image because the debanding is applied to a linear-encoded value instead of the expected nonlinear sRGB encoded value. The debanding function can be seen to assume an 8-bit quantization, in our case to nonlinear sRGB, at [this line of the function that divides by 255.0](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5abed52fd9d99c4aab7d8c62d505f9ad618e4533/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/tonemap.glsl#L825). This is obviously a minor issue, but the behaviour with HDR 2D enabled is not the intended behaviour of this debanding function.

### Steps to reproduce

- Enable debanding or apply a Color Correction adjustment
- Enable and disable HDR 2D to see there is an unexpected difference in the rendered image

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[color-correction-debanding-hdr2d.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20823656/color-correction-debanding-hdr2d.zip)

# Discussion of solutions

Solving the debanding issue is pretty trivial: debanding should simply only ever be applied directly before quantization.

For color correction, one extremely simple solution that has an impact on performance is to simply apply nonlinear sRGB encoding before color correction and convert back to linear encoding before returning from the tonemapping shader. For reference, [I've implemented a quick prototype in a branch of my fork](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...allenwp:godot:vulkan-nonlinear-color-correction-dithering). In the case of color correction and HDR 2D being enabled, this will apply clamping to [0, 1] that wasn't there before -- but I think it makes sense to have this clamping if you're using color correction.
